items.title: EU drafts curbs targeting addictive social media features and AI chatbots - report
items.summary: Investing.com -- European Union regulators are preparing a fresh legislative assault on digital platforms, targeting addictive design mechanics and conversational artificial intelligence designed to drive compulsive engagement. The draft measures, part of an upcoming "Digital Fairness Act" reported by Bloomberg News, would mandate that tech companies allow adult users to disable features that encourage excessive use while also reining in AI chatbots that simulate personal relationships.

items.title: Nvidia intervention preceded transfer of chip probe to Justice Department
items.summary: Investing.com -- Nvidia’s efforts to communicate with U.S. officials over a suspected chip-smuggling investigation preceded an unusual decision to transfer the case from the Commerce Department to the Justice Department, raising new questions about the company’s influence over export-control enforcement.

items.title: Analysts say Nvidia CEO unlikely to be ousted over affair, but raise questions about company's future
items.summary: Analysts on Wall Street say the Nvidia CEO's job is likely safe, but that his affair could increase scrutiny of the company.

items.title: Nvidia Probe Into CEO's Affair Raises Troubling Questions for AI
items.summary: Nvidia Corp., the world's second-most valuable company and the US chipmaker at the heart of the global AI industry, is facing a crisis like none other in its three-decade history. On Nov. 8, Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang admitted he had been unfaithful in his marriage, effectively confirming a series of reports linking him romantically with a woman who has been identified as a suspected Chinese spy and whose company bought chips from Nvidia. Michael Shepard, Bloomberg News Senior Technology Editor, discusses the controversy surrounding Jensen Huang as well as news from the New York Times that Nvidia intervened in the US probe of Megaspeed.

items.title: Barrick Mining Moves on Earnings; Google's New AI Chips | Stock Movers
items.summary: On this episode of Stock Movers: - Shares of Barrick Mining (B) rose in premarket trading after the miner reported third-quarter earnings that beat the average analyst estimate as strength in gold offset copper weakness. The company also said that its Nevada Gold Mines initial public offering remains on track for late 2026 or early 2027. - Shares of Alphabet (GOOG) edged higher after news Google is rolling out a broader array of AI chips, aiming to capitalize on its rapid ascent as a challenger to Nvidia. The company is introducing two new variations of its tensor processing units, or TPUs, custom-made semiconductors that help run AI software. - Shares of KKR & Co. (KKR) rallied in the early session after the company reported a third-quarter profit that beat analysts' estimates as the "mini Berkshire" unit that holds long-term private equity bets mitigated a slump at its Global Atlantic insurance arm.
